schema_conformance.note: The seam every observation in this series records: contracts/participant-observation.schema.json sets additionalProperties false and admits none of the six top-level fields the landing gate reads.

method.independence: Own read-only worktree detached at the pinned commit, git status --porcelain empty at start and finish. Did not grade the shared working tree, which carried 21 paths ahead of the subject. No helper recruited.
own_method: Pinned commit, parent and tree hash before reading anything, and confirmed a single parent.
Ran verify.py twice against trap T6, and lint.py, recording each command's own exit code.
Ran all 60 corpus cases through audit.violations directly rather than reading the test's verdict.
Measured derives_from_agent_result over 104 schema-shaped constants and ten inert expressions, to test the resolver in the direction that convicts correct code.
Compared the frame's rendering against the delivered bytes of both loop dispatches.
Used node to confirm which binding JavaScript actually resolves for each constructed defeat.

observed.scope: 40 files. No undeclared path, no declared-but-unchanged path, no path outside the ten grant prefixes and no excluded_paths entry touched.
observed.accounting_nit: The account says eight modules under scripts/sovprompts/; nine files were added, eight modules plus __init__.py.

reproduced: All 60 corpus cases fire, and all 60 fire on the refusal they declare; none passes only on an unrelated violation. Ids run D1..D60 contiguous.

derives_from_agent_result is free of false positives on the pristine tree: 104 schema-shaped constants across 23 workflows, zero flagged; ten inert expressions all False. The BUILD_SCHEMA collision is genuinely closed.
Identity holds as a fact about the committed artifact: both sov-loop.js dispatches deliver text beginning with the 3385-character frame rendering.
The landing-gate tightening is real and doubly cased: four new OBSERVER_NOT_INDEPENDENT refusals, each with a positive and a defeating case.

defeats.shows: The identity claim is not enforced: the frame reader binds the first textual declaration and never asks which binding executes.
defeats.mechanism: render._body searches for the first `function witnessFrame(`. The package refuses a twice-written binding everywhere else - calls._declared_type refuses a name written twice and a duplicate agentType key - and that rule was never applied to the frame.
defeats.mutation: `witnessFrame = function (...)` reassigned at top level after the declaration, returning a prompt with no subject pin that names the build report the evaluator's oracle.
defeats.result: violations(live()) returned none; both test modules exit 0; python3 scripts/verify.py exit 0 with PASS: 64 checks. node confirms the reassignment is what a call resolves to.

defeats.mechanism: A second `function witnessFrame(...)` after the first; ECMA-262 hoisting takes the last, and every rule grades the first.
defeats.mutation: A duplicate frame declaration returning a prompt that takes the builder's subject and scope as given.
defeats.result: violations(live()) returned none; both test modules exit 0. node confirms the duplicate declaration is what resolves.

residuals: Eleven refusal messages in scripts/sovprompts/ have no case in the corpus and none in the provenance module that fires them. The package's own docstrings invoke SDLC.md gate 3 against undemonstrated refusals.

The weaker rule is narrower than the claim: the demotion requirement fires only when a prompt splices at least one expression, so three of thirty delivered prompts carry no demotion sentence and pass - sov-backlog.js, sov-compression.js and sov-epic.js, each splice-free.
The disclaimed limit reproduces as stated: a prompt opening on the demotion and countermanding it in later prose is not refused. Recorded, not counted against the claim.

authority.observation_basis reads a caller-supplied boolean as a declaration. Disclosed in the docstring, structurally justified because the kernel reads no files, and it gates nothing - it labels a ledger row. A seam, not a defect.
Advisory: DEBT no wall-clock grade at 28.561s, 13 checks over their ceiling. Attributed debt, does not refuse (decisions/0081).
judgement_items: The frame reader binds by first textual declaration while the package refuses a twice-written binding everywhere else. Is closing that asymmetry required inside this concern before WITNESSED, or accepted as named debt under SDLC.md gate 4?
Eleven refusal messages ship with no defeating case. Does SDLC.md gate 3 bind a refusal the package wrote pre-emptively, or only ones a reading actually defeated?
Should a splice-free witness prompt be exempt from carrying the demotion sentence, given three shipped dispatches rely on that exemption?
standing_reason: The work is built, self-tested and green, and most of what it claims reproduces under independent measurement. BUILT -> WITNESSED is withheld: the claim's load-bearing element, that sov-loop.js is held to identity, is falsified by two constructions that keep verify.py at exit 0 while the evaluator receives no subject pin and the build report as its oracle.
